subject: general
question: The marked price of a touchscreen tablet is ₹500. It sells with two successive discounts of 20% and 25%. An additional 19% discount is given on cash payment. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the touchscreen tablet on cash payment?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Selling Price (SP)** = MP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% × (100 − d₃)%

SP = 500 × (80 ÷ 100) × (75 ÷ 100) × (81 ÷ 100)

SP = 500 × (4 ÷ 5) × (3 ÷ 4) × (81 ÷ 100)

SP = 3 × 81 = 243.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹243.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marked Price (MP) = ₹500, Discounts = 20%, 25%, and 19% (on cash).
**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f12484848f736541f28b4d75c906a86f37af0609ff1188729597e68f55b03d3e.png] 
⇒ Price after 1st discount = 500 × (100 − 20) ÷ 100 = 500 × 0.80 = **₹400**.
⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 400 × (100 − 25) ÷ 100 = 400 × 0.75 = **₹300**.
⇒ Price after 3rd (cash) discount = 300 × (100 − 19) ÷ 100 = 300 × 0.81 = **₹243**.
⇒ Final Selling Price = **₹243**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹243.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are applied one after another, the net discount is calculated on the reducing balance. Formula for two discounts: a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price & Selling Price

Marked Price is the price printed on the product. Selling Price is the actual price after deducting all applicable discounts from the Marked Price.
